chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Habib al-Kha'thami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the night prayer in the month of Ramadan, then become junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), then deliberately delay the bath until the dawn breaks.

key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: Becomes junub (enters state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay the ritual bath (ghusl) until dawn during Ramadan if one is in a state of major impurity?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the Prophet’s (saw) voluntary practice of delaying ghusl until dawn after night prayers, establishing a distinction between the permissibility of delaying the bath and the obligation of performing it before the Fajr prayer time. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that the fast remains valid even if one remains in a state of major impurity (junub) throughout the day, provided ghusl is completed before the Adhan of Fajr. This practice underscores the flexibility in ritual purity routines during Ramadan nights.
